jane_corp-sam: Hi team — right after our IdP pushed updated metadata this morning, many users see 'SAML response signature invalid' when signing in to the Console. Some users intermittently succeed. This started at ~08:10 our side. Can you advise?

emma: Sorry to hear that. Are they rotating signing keys (old+new present) or removing the old key? Can you paste the KeyDescriptor section from the metadata or attach the raw XML?

jane_corp-sam: They said they uploaded metadata that contains both the old and new signing keys. Here's the relevant snippet (redacted):

```xml
<EntityDescriptor ...>
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>
        <X509Data>
          <X509Certificate>MIIB...OLDCERT...==</X509Certificate>
        </X509Data>
      </KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>
        <X509Data>
          <X509Certificate>MIIB...NEWCERT...==</X509Certificate>
        </X509Data>
      </KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```

emma: Thanks. Can you also paste the exact error shown in our auth logs when a login fails? If you don't want to share prod logs here, a redacted snippet is fine.

jane_corp-sam: Redacted log snippet from our debug capture: 

```
[auth] 2026-03-17T08:12:34Z ERROR SAML verify: signature verification failed: no certificate matched signature key info
[auth] 2026-03-17T08:12:34Z INFO Attempted cert fingerprints: sha256:AB:...:CD, sha256:EF:...:12
```

emma: That 'no certificate matched' + attempted fingerprints line is interesting. Our SAML verifier tries to match the Signature's KeyInfo to the certificates in metadata; if KeyInfo is absent or KeyName ambiguous, we fall back to trying each candidate. Intermittent success suggests sometimes the Assertion is signed by the new key while our routing/metadata cache still uses the old cert first.

raj: Quick hypothesis — the IdP published both keys but removed KeyName/X509SubjectName info, and the signature itself only contains a KeyValue hint that's ambiguous. Also some IdPs reorder KeyDescriptor elements during auto-deploys, which breaks naive first-match heuristics. Are you behind a multi-region proxy that might be hitting different metadata caches?

jane_corp-sam: We're on a single region but we do have two SSO agents that poll metadata independently. They both fetched the new metadata within minutes. We see about ~30% of logins succeed — likely depending on which agent validated the signature.

emma: For a quick workaround, can the IdP sign with the old key for a short window while we force-refresh our metadata cache? Two options:
- IdP revert to signing with old cert for 15-30m while we invalidate caches server-side.
- IdP add explicit <KeyName> entries or include x509SubjectName so signature KeyInfo matches deterministically.

raj: Long term fix on our side: we should try all candidate certs when verifying signatures rather than stopping on first mismatch and also log which certificate (fingerprint) succeeded/failed. I'll open a follow-up ticket to improve heuristics. For immediate repro, can you attach a full SAMLResponse (base64) from a failing attempt? We can run it against both certs locally with the SAML toolkit to confirm which one verifies.

jane_corp-sam: Uploading the base64 blob privately to the ticket. Also FYI the IdP team said the new cert uses SHA-256 while the old was SHA-1. Could algorithm mismatches cause issues?

emma: SHA-1 vs SHA-256 shouldn't be a problem for our verifier as long as signature uses the corresponding digest algorithm. But if the signature explicitly references a digest algorithm not supported by our runtime, we would see a different error. Your logs show 'no certificate matched', which points at KeyInfo->cert mapping rather than digest acceptance.

oliver: (product) Thanks — tracking this as SUP-2318. We should add clearer diagnostics in the UI/error messages (e.g., include the signing cert fingerprint and 'candidate certs' list). Also consider a cache invalidation endpoint we can call for emergencies.

emma: Next steps agreed:
1) jane_corp-sam: share failing SAMLResponse (done, sent to SUP-2318).
2) IdP: temporarily sign with old key or add KeyName/x509SubjectName in metadata.
3) raj: run local verify against both certs, and log which cert was used. Post results into the ticket.
4) emma/oliver: add short-term doc for customers about ephemeral dual-key rotations and recommended metadata fields.

sso-bot: Ticket SUP-2318 created by emma — assigned to raj. Priority: high. :rotating_light:

jane_corp-sam: Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround.

emma: We'll update SUP-2318 with findings. If you see anything else, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
